hard_fails.invariant: A buyer-selected service add-on must price into the checkout total and the stored order, regardless of which add-on index is selected.
hard_fails.actual: When exactly one add-on is selected and it happens to be the FIRST add-on configured on the service (index 0), it is silently dropped from checkout: no line item appears in Order Summary, the Pay button amount is unchanged, and the resulting order has no add-on. Root cause: src/Integrations/Standalone/StandaloneCheckoutProvider.php line 362 does `if ( $addon_ids_raw )` where `$addon_ids_raw` can legitimately be the PHP string "0" (the sole selected add-on's index) -- PHP treats the string "0" as falsy, so the entire add-on-resolution block is skipped. The same falsy check appears at line 299 for the cart-fallback branch. Selecting any other single index (e.g. addons=1) or multiple indices including 0 (e.g. addons=0,1) works correctly because the string is then non-"0" and therefore truthy. Since most vendors configure only one add-on, this is the single most common real-world case for the release's headline feature.

top3: HARD FAIL: selecting a lone add-on at index 0 (the most common real-world case -- a service with exactly one add-on) is silently dropped from the checkout total and the stored order, because of a PHP falsy-string bug (`if ($addon_ids_raw)` treats the string "0" as empty) in StandaloneCheckoutProvider.php lines 299 and 362. This breaks the release's headline add-ons feature for its most common configuration.

Site data issue (not plugin code): wpss_order_confirmation_page is set to page 796, a leftover 'QA Thank You' test page with no order details, sidebar widgets full of Factory Post junk, and no link back to the order or dashboard -- every buyer who pays lands there instead of a real confirmation screen. The underlying fallback code (wpss_get_post_checkout_url()) is correct when this option is unset; clearing it (or repointing it to a real page) before any further checkout QA is required.

Minor UI inconsistency: the admin 'Mark as Paid' button (OfflineGateway.php ~line 988) uses a native browser confirm() dialog instead of the plugin's own themed WPSS.showConfirm()/wpssConfirm pattern used elsewhere (e.g. the service wizard's remove-extra/remove-FAQ actions). Not a functional defect, but inconsistent with the plugin's established UI language.

failures.triage_note: Root-caused precisely to a PHP truthiness bug, not a data or config issue. Reproduced on both the /service-checkout/{id}/ rewrite route and the mapped ?service={id} page, so both checkout renderers share the same underlying add-on resolution bug.
failures.expected: Selecting the service's only add-on (Priority Support, +$25.00) via the on-page 'Order Options' modal and clicking Continue to Checkout should show Order Summary as Basic $59.99 + Priority Support $25.00 = Total $84.99, and the Pay button should read 'Pay $84.99'.
failures.actual: Order Summary shows only 'Basic $59.99', Total $59.99, and 'Pay $59.99' -- the add-on and its $25.00 are completely absent from the page and from the hidden addon_ids/addons_data form fields (both empty/missing). Confirmed the same when navigating directly to /service-checkout/2028/?package=0&addons=0 and to /service-checkout/?service=2028&package=0&addons=0. Confirmed the add-on IS carried through correctly when: (a) a different single index is used (addons=1 on service 2026 worked, total $99.98 correctly included the $19.99 Extra Revisions add-on), and (b) two indices including 0 are used together (addons=0,1 worked, total $149.97). Completed a full purchase on a fresh 2-addon test service (ID 2215, 'QA Free Limits Test Service 0923B') with addons=0,1 selected and it round-tripped perfectly into wpss_orders: subtotal 45.00, addons_total 25.00 (Rush Delivery $15 + Source Files Package $10), total 70.00, commission_rate 10%, platform_fee 7.00, vendor_earnings 63.00, payment_method 'offline' (not NULL).

failures.triage_note: Site/test-data configuration issue, not a code defect. wp option get wpss_order_confirmation_page returns 796, which is a page titled 'QA Thank You' with post_content literally 'Thanks' -- clearly leftover from an earlier QA session on this same site. Code path (wpss_get_post_checkout_url() in src/functions/orders.php) is correct: when the option is 0/unset it falls back to the real order-view URL. Recommend clearing wp option delete wpss_order_confirmation_page (or pointing it at a real page) before any further buyer-journey QA on this site, since every completed order currently redirects here.
